identity.description:
Set diff-bugs and security to one pass by E7, fix the verifier budget throw, and raise the verifier caps

## Summary

E7 of D4c from the S1 reference run, and two fixes that S1 found. Version 0.17.0.

- **E7: diff-bugs and security go to one pass.** On S1 (28 cases, one repeat, `eval-report --by-pass`, no model call), both fail test (b) of the D8 rule:
  - diff-bugs: a second pass added 2 goldens at $7.15 for each added golden, against $0.58 for each golden of one pass. R is 12.4, and the upper end of its interval is 63.5.
  - security: a second pass added 3 goldens at $2.89 for each, against $0.61. R is 4.8, and its interval has no upper end.
  - Test (c) passes for both.
  - Every built-in reviewer now runs one pass. A repo sets `reviewers.<name>.passes` to buy a second pass.
- **E7: the cross-pass dedupe key stays.** A second pass gave 38 claims on a span and a category that the first pass also gave. None of them matched a golden that no other finding matched.
- **The budget throw.** In S1, a verifier call threw "Reached maximum budget ($0.5)" instead of returning the limit subtype. The client counted the throw as a failed call, so the review was incomplete and the eval repeat failed. Now a thrown budget or turn-limit stop gives the failure kind `limit`, for every role, so the finding ends unsure and the review completes (`src/sdk/client.ts`).
- **The verifier caps go up:** a verifier call from $0.50 to $1, and an escalation from $1 to $2. In S1, the first verifier has a 99th percentile of $0.40 and a maximum of $0.42, and the escalation reached $0.999. A cap costs nothing until a call reaches it. The principal decided this change.
- **`replay --verifier-cap <usd>`** sets the cap of an arm, for the Opus arms of E3. The report counts the capped calls of each arm.
- **`replay --judge-cache <dir>`** gives the arms of one experiment a shared judge cache, so a second arm asks nothing again.
- The help and the README now say that `--arm stored` makes no verifier call but can ask the judge for the golden match.
- The note is `docs/research/e7-passes-dedupe.md`. It also gives the E3 figures from S1: 135 of 239 verifications escalated (56%), the escalation changed 28 of them (21%), and the escalations cost $47.81 against $39.99 for the first verifier.

## Spend

S1 cost $165.00 on the plan login: $159.02 for the 28 cases, and $5.98 for one failed attempt of injection-walle-6, which is the budget throw above. The E7 analysis made no model call. Two runs of `replay --arm stored` asked the judge for about $2.80 together. The records of S1 are in the crew record root, outside the repo.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` (1687 tests), `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`
- [x] `scripts/check-version-bump.sh cec32f7 HEAD` gives 0.16.0 to 0.17.0
- [x] The red commits 0394d03 (the budget throw) and 1fb3757 (`--verifier-cap`) fail before their fixes
- [x] The tests that need two passes now set them, and no assertion became weaker

triage.summary: This is the 0.17.0 release. It drops diff-bugs and security to one pass by default, based on the E7 analysis. It doubles the verifier and escalation dollar caps, and a thrown SDK budget or turn limit error now counts as a limit stop that ends unsure. It adds `--verifier-cap` and `--judge-cache` to replay, a `capped` figure, docs, and test updates.

finding.claim: No test checks that saveCache keeps the answers that another arm already wrote to the shared judge cache.
finding.evidence: for (const [k, v] of state.cache) merged.set(k, v);
finding.suggested_fix: Seed the shared cache file with an extra key, run one arm, then assert that the key is still in the file.
finding.explanation: The test of the shared cache runs two arms that ask the same questions, so it still passes if the code overwrites the file instead of merging into it.

quotes: for (const [k, v] of state.cache) merged.set(k, v);
first.rationale: The only --judge-cache test (test/replay-cap.test.ts) runs two arms against one shared cache and checks that the second arm makes no judge call. It never seeds the shared file with a key from another arm. A change that overwrote the shared file instead of merging would still pass.

quotes: for (const [k, v] of state.cache) merged.set(k, v);
if (existsSync(shared)) for (const [k, v] of await readJudgeCache(shared)) cache.set(k, v);
escalated.rationale: It is true that no test checks the merge: the only shared-cache test runs two arms one after the other and checks that the second asks the judge nothing. But each arm loads the shared file into state.cache before it writes, so an overwrite would keep the other arm's keys too. The merge only matters when two arms write at the same time, and the suggested test would pass even if the code overwrote the file, so the finding is not worth the author's time.
